decision: Extend the existing native local path with a mandatory scoped LocalEnvironment branch and one shared ProcessRegistry supervised launch/settlement path. Keep native bash, snapshot scripts, foreground output, background/PTY readers, process_manage and receipts. One transient user service plus bubblewrap per command/session; no new broker, daemon, shell interpreter, scheduler, Harness/A0 worker or shared stop domain.

existing_native_hooks.role: Current local factory always returns ordinary LocalEnvironment; select scoped subclass here from authenticated internal binding, retain env_type local.
Native terminal and lazy file-tool bring-up share this factory; identity must survive both paths.

Dispatch scoped custody to exact-unit settlement, before general host PID/PGID paths.
Existing checkpoint-before-launch, gated child, mandatory transient service and actual activation deadline validation are reusable lifecycle patterns.
Existing exact invocation/cgroup identity and retained STOP_UNCONFIRMED pattern; not a ready shell method.
Reuse native recovery store; recover shell custody intent even without live wrapper PID.
Native bounded retained receipt; parent adds immutable user_authority here and in load.
Current generic non-timeout exception retry re-executes up to three times; scoped submit errors must bypass it.

source_facts.fact: ContextVar scopes TERMINAL_* configuration only. It is not process, filesystem, credential or network isolation.
_make_run_env starts from os.environ and can include desktop DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY/DBUS; scoped shell must construct an explicit environment instead.
Legacy _scope_argv uses optional systemd --scope and falls back to host bash. It lacks mandatory finite RuntimeMaxSec and mount containment.
PTY spawn exceptions can fall back to pipe execution. For a scoped submission with possible effects this risks replay and must be disabled.
_run_foreground retries general exceptions. Launch uncertainty is not a transient retry permission.
Web lifecycle establishes intent, mandatory service, bounded startup, hard deadline verified against ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic, and input fence.
Child only admits web_search/web_extract and imports native web implementations; it does not execute arbitrary shell and must remain web-specific.
Checkpoint writes swallow failures. Scoped launch needs strict write/readback and durable filesystem acknowledgement before release, not ordinary best-effort persistence.
Existing retained receipt schema has no user principal or access generation. Parent owns adding user_authority to live, checkpoint and retained records.

NativeSupervisor observes/stops a pre-owned transient user service; it does not launch, impose mounts, or supply terminal transport. Its Description format is Friday rework plus admission hash, different from web.
Existing bwrap allowlisted-root construction and env replacement demonstrate available source design, but the adapter itself invokes Harness and must not become ordinary terminal execution.
Installer bwrap binds the host root; it provides lifetime custody, not principal filesystem isolation. Do not reuse this argv verbatim for arbitrary user shell.
Plugin providers cannot shadow local. A plugin backend alone routes background work to spawn_via_env, whose source has no stdin/PTY. Native local extension is the smaller complete route.

proposed_source_contract.authority_owner: Parent implements immutable user_authority and protected process_manage visibility. Backend consumes that exact representation, never introduces an alternative authority store.
binding_fields: user_authority principal/profile/home directory identity/binding hash/access generation
raw originating task ID and current authorized owner task ID
parent native session ID and session key
turn/call correlation key and launch generation for deduplication
original task deadline monotonic plus boot ID and original budget provenance
call execution timeout cap, admitted aggregate resource allocation, mount-root identities, explicit environment/network policy
sticky stop/revocation fence and immutable launch-intent digest

ProcessRegistry.settle_scoped_local(self, session: ProcessSession, *, stop: bool = False) -> dict
proposed_source_contract.signatures_note: These are proposed internal hooks, not claims of existing APIs. TerminalBinding is an immutable projection of parent user_authority plus existing native task/deadline state; command arguments cannot construct it.
factory_and_foreground: In _build_local_env, select ScopedLocalEnvironment whenever product authority is engaged; missing, stale, unsupported or unbound capability refuses. Keep env_type local so terminal background/PTY/yield semantics remain native. Propagate binding through _create_configured_env and lazy ensure_task_env; env-cache key includes principal/profile/access generation/raw task ownership, not cwd alone.

Bind before LocalEnvironment.__init__ calls init_session. Override _run_bash to use spawn_scoped_local(foreground=True), return the existing Popen-compatible service wrapper, and attach its existing registry session identity. Register/checkpoint custody before Popen; do not start a second registry reader while BaseEnvironment owns stdout.

Reuse BaseEnvironment snapshot bootstrap/wrap scripts. Scoped get_temp_dir returns only a private mounted shell-state directory; scoped initial/recovered cwd stays within explicit admitted mounts. Override shell-init handling so host login rc, shell_init_files and _make_run_env never run or leak ambient environment.

Keep bound workspace/state paths identical inside and outside namespace where practical so existing cwd and file-tool behavior works; create empty ancestors rather than bind entire profile/home. Only workspace, private terminal home/state and explicitly admitted extra roots are exposed.

Wrap _wait_for_process to settle before reporting actual exit; a successful yield transfers the same session, wrapper, cgroup, invocation, deadline and stop bit to the native background reader. No replacement process or new budget.

Scoped _kill_process/_kill_spawned_tree/cleanup use exact owned service. Hard-exit _force_kill_process can only dispatch bounded stop and retain pending intent; it cannot claim quiescence without observation. Systemd original deadline still enforces lifetime after gateway death.
background_and_pty: Extend terminal_tool_background._spawn local branch to pass env.binding into mandatory scoped registry spawn. Put the scoped branch ahead of legacy spawn_local/_scope_argv fallback. Generic spawn_via_env is not this route.

Background pipe uses systemd-run --user --pipe --wait and existing Popen/_reader_loop. Preserve stdin as a pipe for process write/submit/close rather than legacy DEVNULL. PTY uses existing PtyProcess wrapping systemd-run --user --pty --wait and _pty_reader_loop.

The PTY is allocated by the dedicated transient service transport, not inherited from a gateway/user terminal. For that PTY route do not blindly apply bwrap --new-session, which can detach its controlling terminal. Validate actual controlling TTY, EOF, signal and job-control behavior before acceptance; failure refuses, with no pipe retry.

Background initialization takes a stable copy of the native foreground shell snapshot into process-owned state, preserving useful exports/functions/aliases without concurrent writers replacing the foreground snapshot. A PTY retains its own in-process shell/REPL state. Native foreground snapshot semantics remain intact.

adopt_local reuses the already registered scoped custody session and seeds output exactly once. _finish_reader/_reconcile_local_exit cannot publish completion until native wrapper has ended AND recorded cgroup is empty; output EOF alone is insufficient.

poll/log/wait/list/handoff/retained queries use parent authority guard. write/submit/close also check sticky stop and generation immediately before bounded nonblocking I/O; no blocking flush can exceed the original process deadline. Handoff keeps immutable originating principal/generation/deadline and separately records authorized owner transfer.
persist_on_release may survive ordinary turn release only under its existing durable owner and original deadline. It never overrides /stop, /new, revoke, cancel or unknown custody.
supervisor_reuse: Factor the small web launch/checkpoint/observation/settlement mechanics into a custody-kind-neutral helper used by ProcessRegistry; keep WebProcessMixin and web_process_child behavior unchanged. Shell-specific state must not masquerade as web_custody.

Match NativeSupervisor identity discipline: protected admission digest in Description, unique immutable service name, Transient=yes, InvocationID continuity, original ControlGroup path plus device/inode, whole-cgroup KillMode=control-group and SendSIGKILL=yes. NativeSupervisor alone lacks the deadline/resource checks, so include those in shell launch observation.

Mandatory service policy: Type=exec, RemainAfterExit=no, ExitType=main, Restart=no, RuntimeRandomizedExtraSec=0, TimeoutStartSec=3s, TimeoutStopSec<=1s, NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectControlGroups=yes, Delegate=no, UMask=0077, explicitly admitted MemoryMax/CPUQuota/TasksMax. Do not use --scope or delegate cgroup management to shell.

Use original D and the existing conservative 3s startup/4s settlement reserves; set RuntimeMaxSec from remaining time minus both reserves, then verify actual ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic + RuntimeMaxUSec <= D - settlement reserve. Never reset D on foreground promotion, adoption, recovery, handoff or process interaction. Reject insufficient startup budget before effects.

Settle validates exact unit/invocation and retained cgroup identity; only wrapper gone plus empty/removed original cgroup establishes QUIESCENT. Keep STOP_UNCONFIRMED custody otherwise. Strict parser rejects duplicate/missing/contradictory systemctl and cgroup fields; current web dict parsing alone is not sufficient.
mount_and_environment_policy: Build fixed bwrap argv from authenticated policy, using the existing DSH allowlisted-mount pattern only: unshare user/pid/ipc/uts and network for initial local-only capability, cap-drop ALL, private proc/dev/tmp with explicit tmp size, read-only /usr/toolchain/pinned launch helper, declared writable workspace/private shell home/state, root remount read-only. No host / bind, whole profile home, credential files, /run/user, Docker socket, host proc or writable cgroup mount.

Initial shell has no network namespace access to host loopback/abstract sockets. Authorized web work remains available through existing native web tools. A future shell network grant must reuse a separately proven explicit network boundary; it cannot silently inherit gateway network.

systemd control wrapper gets only explicit PATH/LANG and trusted user bus location. Inside bwrap use --clearenv and explicit shell PATH/HOME/TMPDIR/locale; no DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, launch .env, provider secrets, DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY, LD_PRELOAD or ambient BASH_ENV. Profile passthrough is not a credentials grant.

NoNewPrivileges/capability drop deny host sudo. Preserve ordinary native command approvals for destructive actions within admitted mounts; force approval is never authority expansion. Do not request a sudo password for a namespace that cannot use it.

Binding checks actual root directory identities and safe mount construction before launch and reuse. cwd is a command location, not the security boundary. Missing workspace may fall back only to the same admitted workspace root, never os.getcwd() or gateway home.
one_shot_release_gate: A tiny pinned one-shot launch gate is necessary because arbitrary bash must not execute before unit identity/deadline/checkpoint are acknowledged. This gate has no shell evaluator, persistent loop or scheduling API: validate fixed bounded input, wait once under D, then os.execve the existing /usr/bin/bash with the native wrapped command.

Launch gate inside already constructed bwrap. Before release it emits one bounded READY line with the launch nonce through the same native pipe/PTY, and consumes exactly one fixed EXEC line without buffering subsequent application stdin. Parent strips the READY frame, validates service/cgroup/deadline and strict checkpoint, then writes EXEC once under the sticky fence. Record release intent before writing; a torn write or lost acknowledgement is UNKNOWN, not permission to replay.

For PTY, gate must disable echo during control handshake and restore terminal mode before exec; subsequent process writes are normal native PTY bytes. For pipe mode preserve exact caller stdin after the gate line and close when foreground stdin is exhausted. Handshake/read/write budgets fit startup/original D. EOF, mismatch or deadline before release exits without executing command.

Command/argv is data held by the trusted gate until release; do not modify web_process_child to run it. All manager arguments use argv arrays and --expand-environment=no. The gate adds only safe invocation glue permitted by the V2 reuse rule.
recovery_and_results: Persist scoped custody discriminator, user_authority, task/owner/session identity, original D/boot, launch intent/release state, exact unit/invocation/cgroup identity and stop bit in the existing checkpoint. Require fd/directory synchronization and readback before release; plain best-effort _write_checkpoint is insufficient.

Recover the same intent even if no PID was saved or wrapper PID is gone/reused. Service deadline remains independent while gateway is absent. Reconcile exact recorded service/cgroup; never spawn again automatically. Expired records do not get another work budget; later recovery is bounded observation/stop only.

Original pipes/PTY cannot be restored by current native recovery. Minimal supported policy: recover status/log receipts and exact stop capability, mark stdin unavailable, settle lost-transport sessions rather than claim live PTY reconnection. Preserve durable workspace and bounded already captured output; do not claim complete post-crash output.

Retained native result records include parent user_authority and final boundary observation. Parent reader/visibility validation must exclude foreign/stale generation and ambiguous prefix matches. Preserve output redaction and avoid replay as notifications.

Trusted stop/cleanup retains checked custody after principal revocation and does not need renewed user admission; new effects and process stdin do. Completion, stop acknowledgement, release of capacity and pruning require actual settlement. Unknown rows block new conflicting launches.

bounded_stage_order: 1 Resolve trusted native caller/task and immutable user_authority; retain original deadline. Validate local-only capability, resource allocation, mount identities and no existing unknown conflicting custody.
2 Preserve native approval flow and stop fence. Prepare private shell state and bounded command metadata; install immutable environment binding before trusted snapshot bootstrap.
3 Allocate unique ProcessSession/service identity in existing registry; durably checkpoint INTENT before invoking systemd. Stop racing with checkpoint must prevent launch.
4 Launch exactly once with fixed service hard deadline/resources plus bwrap and inert one-shot gate. Await gate readiness and manager identity only within bounded startup window.
5 Verify actual invocation, original cgroup identity, resource/deadline properties; strict checkpoint; revalidate authority and sticky stop; persist release intent; send one permit.
6 Native foreground drain or background/PTY reader runs normal bash. Promotion/adoption retains the exact same custody. All further process input and output access use appropriate authority fences.
7 On natural exit, cancellation, deadline, revoke, loss or setup uncertainty, latch stop as required; observe/stop exact unit, verify wrapper and cgroup cessation, retain unknown otherwise.
8 Only after quiescence publish native result/retained receipt, release capacity and cleanup eligible scratch. Recovery performs observation of the same intent, never implicit re-execution.
mandatory_source_changes_before_enable: Wire both LocalEnvironment foreground and ProcessRegistry background/PTY to the same mandatory launcher; patch native adoption and finalization.
Make original deadline and allocation explicit at trusted ingress and persisted in existing records; independent service timer must cover gateway loss.
Disable scoped generic execution retry, PTY pipe fallback, bare host spawn fallback, host cwd recovery, ambient login rc/env and host generic kill fallbacks.
Enforce immutable principal/access generation on cached environment, live and retained process lookup, mutations, stdin, handoff and durable receipts while keeping trusted cleanup independent.
Preserve native snapshot and process APIs with bounded I/O, strict checkpoint durability, sticky stop and launch uncertainty fencing.
Only then propose terminal/process_manage additions to SAFE and profile tool grants. This route and the parent principal-only slice authorize no such enablement.
required_real_tests: Small native terminal command and file transformation in admitted workspace; exact output/exit; foreground cd/export/function/alias state across calls; safe missing-cwd behavior; existing native approval denied/approved/force semantics.

Background pipe output, bounded tail/retained result, write/submit/close; PTY true isatty/controlling-terminal, REPL state, stdin/EOF, Ctrl-C and resize where native API supports it. No mode fallback or duplicate command after PTY startup failure.
Foreground yield/promote/adopt: same service/invocation/process session/deadline, one reader, no duplicate output/notification or command; background snapshot does not clobber foreground state.

Cross-principal/profile/access-generation/task/session guessed IDs and ambiguous prefixes rejected for live, finished and disk-retained query and mutation; revoke/re-enable cannot revive old stdin or state; same-principal authorized handoff retains original deadline.

Credential env/file sentinel, other profile/workspace, symlink/cwd escapes, host proc/cgroup/systemd/socket/SSH agent/sudo and loopback/abstract-network escape attempts have no access or side effects. Native web tool remains available independently.

Detached setsid/double-fork/SIGTERM-ignoring descendants: explicit kill, active/idle /stop, /new, revoke, hard deadline and gateway SIGKILL all result in exact original cgroup empty by admitted budget; unrelated service survives.

Gateway kept down beyond deadline then recovered: same retained intent, no automatic replay, no false pipes/PTY recovery, honest output loss, independently observed timeout cessation before gateway recovery.

Faults at each intent/Popen/READY/observation/checkpoint/release/reader transition; disk full/write/readback/fsync fault, malformed native fields, user bus unavailable, changed invocation/cgroup, PID reuse, original boot change, late activation and blocked stdin. Each gives refusal or retained STOP_UNCONFIRMED with no fresh budget.

Resource reality: actual CPU/memory/tasks/tmp limits and admitted aggregate concurrency; output flooding, startup wedge and failed stop must not exceed original deadline or corrupt authoritative receipts. Final exact composed source/config artifact needs required independent review and real final gates.
limitations: Source design only: no subject imports, tests, subprocess shell execution through Hermes, native services, model, network or runtime changes occurred. Availability and compatibility of user systemd, unprivileged bwrap and nested PTY behavior remain untested.

Linux scoped local shell only; Windows/SSH/container backends remain outside this bounded route. Native foreground snapshot semantics are preserved, not a claim of a permanently running foreground shell.
Private workspace shell supports ordinary local tasks; it does not grant arbitrary gateway-owner host administration, unrestricted network, credentials or system sudo.
Minimal recovery preserves exact stop/status and durable artifacts, not resurrection of PTY stdin or lossless full stdout after gateway crash.
Parent principal package and this proposal are separate source slices. No SAFE capability enabled, no live owner-runtime acceptance, no paused/stopped attempt resumed.
